eb56b200-b0ab-46ed-b372-eeaa2a712803.solution:
**(a)**
Advantages: When the leaf folds up during wilting, the surface area exposed to sunlight is reduced, so less water is lost through evaporation. In addition, the guard cells become flaccid, causing the stomata to close, which reduces the rate of transpiration (rate of water loss).

Disadvantages: The rate of photosynthesis is reduced because of the reduced surface area exposed to sunlight. Also, as the stomata close, carbon dioxide becomes the limiting factor for photosynthesis.

**(b)**
Adaptation of the root hair cell:
The root hair cell possesses a long, narrow protrusion (extension), which increases its surface area to volume ratio, allowing a faster rate of absorption of water by osmosis.
The cell sap in the root hair cell is concentrated, which lowers the water potential of the cell, so as to establish a steep water potential gradient for water to enter the cell by osmosis.
The root hair cell contains numerous mitochondria, which release energy for the active transport of mineral salts.

30e7eba2-c043-47b8-aaaa-e74d48b6c05f.question_text: Section B, Question 8 - EITHER. (Question 8 is an Either/Or question; only one part should be answered. This row is the EITHER alternative; the OR alternative is stored as question 9.)
30e7eba2-c043-47b8-aaaa-e74d48b6c05f.solution:
(a) Most food molecules are large and insoluble. They are too big to pass through, or diffuse across, the wall of the small intestine (the epithelium of the villus) into the blood. Digestion breaks these large, insoluble molecules down into small, soluble molecules that can be absorbed into the bloodstream and then assimilated by the body cells. This is why most foods must be digested.

(b) Excess amino acids are deaminated in the liver, forming urea. The urea diffuses out of the liver cells into the blood in the hepatic vein. It travels to the vena cava, then to the right atrium and right ventricle of the heart. From there it is pumped through the pulmonary artery to the lungs and returns through the pulmonary vein to the left atrium and left ventricle. It leaves the heart in the aorta and enters the kidney through the renal artery. In the glomerulus, it is filtered out under high pressure (ultrafiltration) into the Bowman's capsule.

daad0efa-a355-4374-9296-3040fb8e2fec.question_text:
Fig. 2.1 shows the position of a person's teeth (comprising incisors and molars), and his masseter muscle used to move the lower jawbone.

Fig. 2.2 shows a simplified model of the lower jawbone of negligible mass. The model consists of two straight parts of length 7.0 cm and 4.0 cm, making an angle of 50° to each other. During one particular bite of a piece of food, a downward force of 45 N is applied on the incisors at the front of the lower jawbone, while an upward muscle force $F$ is exerted by the masseter muscle at the back of the lower jawbone.

parts.text: The lower jawbone is in equilibrium. Determine the magnitude of the muscle force $F$ applied by the masseter muscle.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
By taking moments, sum of clockwise moments = sum of anti-clockwise moments [formula]
$F \times 4.0 \cos 50° = 45 \times 7.0$
$F \times 4.0 \cos 50° = 45 \times 7.0$
$F = 123$ N

parts.text: Hence, determine the magnitude and direction of the force applied on the pivot.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
By Newton's First Law, sum of upward forces = sum of downward forces.
Force on pivot + 45 = 123
Force on pivot = 78 N
Direction = downwards

parts.text: Suggest, for the same moment created by the jawbone, why the molars used for crushing hard food are found at the back, rather than the front of the jaw.
parts.label: c
parts.solution: At the back, molars apply a force on the food whose line of action has a shorter perpendicular distance to the pivot. For the same moment created by $F$, force by molar teeth (on hard) food is larger.

parts.text: Incisors are sharper than molars. Using concepts of pressure, suggest why incisors are used for cutting meat rather than molars for the same force exerted by incisors and molars.
parts.label: d
parts.solution: Incisors have a smaller surface area of contact (with the meat) than molars. For the same force exerted, incisors exert a larger pressure to be able to cut meat.

parts.text: A bubble of carbon dioxide gas rises from the diver to the surface of the sea. State how the volume of the bubble changes as it rises. Explain why using the Kinetic Model of Matter.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
The volume of the bubble increases.
When temperature remains constant, the average kinetic energy of the molecules remains constant.
Since the frequency of collisions must decrease to lower pressure, the volume of the bubble must increase.

$(2 \times 10^7)(0.001) = [(1 \times 10^5) + 2(1 \times 10^5)](V_2)$
$V_2 = 0.0667$ m$^3 = 0.070$ m$^3$

parts.text: Using a named enzyme, explain why the human digestive system needs to produce many different enzymes.
parts.label: a
parts.answer:
Each enzyme is specific in action / can only break down / digest a certain nutrient / substrate due to their unique / specific shape in active site [1].
Since there are many nutrients / substrates to break down / digest in the human digestive system, different enzymes are required to break down these different nutrients [1].
For example, amylase can only break down starch into maltose but is unable to break down other substances [1] (or any other enzyme found in the human digestive system, along with corresponding substrate).
[Take note: Only one example of enzyme and substrate is necessary as mentioned in the question. Reject: Irrelevant example of enzyme and substrate in the context that answer given is out of point.]

parts.text: Some baby foods are manufactured by pre-digesting nutrients found in the foods using digestive enzymes. Suggest why it is necessary to pre-digest baby foods.
parts.label: b
parts.answer:
Babies lack teeth so they are unable to chew food [break up food into small pieces] [1]. [Reject: break food molecules into small(er) molecules]
Pre-digesting food will allow a larger surface area to volume ratio for enzymes to act on [1].
There may not be enough digestive enzymes produced by babies [1].
Pre-digesting food will speed up digestion of complex food substances (nutrients) [1]. [Reject: Babies do not have necessary enzymes.]
[Reject: Answer that is focused on the effects of not giving pre-digested food to babies - out of point]

parts.text: Compare the structures between a molecule of pepsin and a molecule of sucrose.
parts.label: c
parts.answer:
[Answers must include both similarities and differences. 1m for similarity + 2m for differences OR 2m for similarities + 1m for difference]
Similarities [1m each]
- Both molecules consist of more than one basic unit.
- Both molecules contain elements of carbon / hydrogen / oxygen.
Differences [1m each]
- Pepsin contains nitrogen which is absent in sucrose.
- Ratio of carbon to hydrogen in sucrose is 1:2 but there is no such fixed ratio in pepsin.
- Sucrose is made up of two basic units / monomers but pepsin is made up of many basic units joined together.
- Pepsin is a larger molecule than sucrose.
[R: Sucrose is a nutrient but pepsin is an enzyme / Pepsin has a 3-dimensional structure but sucrose does not / Pepsin has an active site but sucrose does not.]

0cb02103-6fce-4268-8de0-fbcb9154583a.solution:
(a) Each enzyme is specific in its action and can only break down / digest a certain nutrient / substrate, due to the unique / specific shape of its active site. Since there are many different nutrients / substrates that need to be broken down / digested in the human digestive system, different enzymes are required to break down these different nutrients. For example, amylase can only break down starch into maltose but is unable to break down other substances (any other valid enzyme–substrate example is acceptable).

(b) Babies lack teeth, so they are unable to chew food / break up food into small pieces. Pre-digesting the food will therefore allow a larger surface area to volume ratio for enzymes to act on. There may not be enough digestive enzymes produced by babies. Pre-digesting the food will speed up the digestion of complex food substances (nutrients).

(c) Similarities:
- Both pepsin and sucrose molecules consist of more than one basic unit.
- Both molecules contain the elements carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.

Differences:
- Pepsin contains nitrogen, which is absent in sucrose.
- The ratio of carbon to hydrogen in sucrose is 1:2, but there is no such fixed ratio in pepsin.
- Sucrose is made up of two basic units / monomers, whereas pepsin is made up of many basic units joined together.
- Pepsin is a larger molecule than sucrose.

**Section B — Answer one question from this section.**

Zamak is an alloy of zinc with magnesium, aluminium and copper. It is widely used to make die-cast toys. Magnesium and aluminium are adjacent elements in the third Period of the Periodic Table. Zinc and copper are next to each other in the first set of transition elements.

Table 11.1 shows the densities of the four metals present in Zamak.

**Table 11.1**

| metal | metal 1 | metal 2 | metal 3 | metal 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| density (g/cm$^3$) | 1.74 | 2.70 | 7.13 | 8.96 |

parts.text: Suggest the identities of metals 3 and 4 present in Zamak.
parts.label: a

subparts.text: When finely powdered Zamak is shaken with cold dilute hydrochloric acid, three of the metals dissolved and one remains as a solid residue. Name the solid residue.
subparts.label: i

subparts.text: Explain, in terms of collision theory, why finely powdered Zamak is used in the reaction.
subparts.label: ii
subparts.solution:
Powdered Zamak has a smaller particle size with a greater surface area exposed to the acid for reaction. [1]

Thus, the frequency of effective collisions increases and the rate of reaction is higher. [1]

parts.text: Using ideas of arrangement of atoms in Zamak alloy, explain why Zamak is harder than pure zinc.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Atoms in pure zinc are of the **same size** and arranged in an **orderly manner**. Layers of atoms can slide over one another. [1]

**Different sizes of atoms** (aluminium, copper and magnesium) in the alloy **disrupt the orderly arrangement**, making it difficult for the **layers of atoms** to slide over one another. [1]

parts.text:
Air is then pumped into the rocket so that the pressure of the air inside the rocket increases.

Explain, in terms of particles, why the air in the rocket exerts a pressure on the walls of the rocket.
parts.label: a
parts.solution:
$B1$: Moving air molecules collide with the inner wall of the container and exerts a force on it.

$B1$: Since pressure is the force exerted per unit area, the air molecules exert pressure on the surface of the wall.

parts.text:
When the air pressure in the rocket is high, the rubber tubing is removed from the rocket. The water in the rocket is expelled downwards.

Use Newton's laws of motion to explain why the rocket begins to accelerate upwards.
parts.label: b
parts.solution:
$B1$: Using Newton's third law, the downwards force of water on the rocket is equal to the upwards force of rocket on water.

$B1$: Using Newton's second law, the upwards force is larger than sum of weight and air resistance. Positive net force is upwards.

parts.text:
As the water is expelled from the rocket, the upward acceleration of the rocket decreases.

Suggest two reasons for the change in the acceleration of the rocket.
parts.label: c
parts.solution:
Any two of the following ($B2$, one mark each):

$B1$: The weight of the rocket decreases.

$B1$: Air resistance increases.

$B1$: Pressure of air in rocket decreases / and so resistance / propulsive force decreases.

$B1$: Less water expelled per second at slower speed.
